#### 1. arterial calcification, generalized, of infancy, 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.715)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:3356)

**Proposed mechanism:** ENPP1 (HGNC:3356) —DISRUPTS→ Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70254); Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70254) —DECREASES→ Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:17206); Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:17206) —INCREASES→ Vascular calcification (REACT:R-HSA-71413); Vascular calcification (REACT:R-HSA-71413) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal vascular calcification (HP:0003187); Vascular calcification (REACT:R-HSA-71413) —LEADS_TO→ Generalized arterial calcification of infancy (HP:0011704). Loss-of-function mutations in ENPP1 lead to decreased production of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi). Elevated PPi is crucial for inhibiting pathological calcification. Reduced PPi levels thus promote vascular calcification, manifesting as generalized arterial calcification of infancy (MONDO:0008817) and contributing to the abnormal vascular calcification seen in MONDO:0014227.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ENPP1 associated with gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in either disease, or demonstration that the two diseases are caused by entirely independent pathways with no convergence on PPi metabolism or vascular calcification. _(variant: rs104899076)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting PPi levels or its regulators could offer a therapeutic strategy for both diseases. Understanding the ENPP1-PPi axis is crucial for developing treatments that prevent or reverse vascular calcification.

Loss-of-function mutations in ENPP1 lead to decreased hydrolysis of pyrophosphate, resulting in its accumulation. Elevated pyrophosphate disrupts phosphate metabolism, leading to impaired bone mineralization and rickets.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with loss-of-function mutations in ENPP1 who do not exhibit abnormal bone mineralization or rickets. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD shows that pathogenic variants in ENPP1 are rare, supporting a role in rare Mendelian diseases.)_
